title: MKV to MP4 – Convert OBS Recordings Free, No Upload
description: Convert MKV files from OBS and downloads to MP4 for phones, TVs and editors. H.264 picture is copied without loss. In your browser, no upload.
heading: Convert MKV to MP4
subtitle: Make an MKV from OBS or a download into an MP4 that phones, TVs and editors open; nothing is uploaded.
intro: OBS records to MKV by default, because a crash mid-recording leaves an MKV that still plays. Many downloads use MKV too. But iPhones, many smart TVs, Premiere and most social sites want MP4. MKV is only the box: inside there is usually H.264 picture, which this page copies straight into an MP4 without re-encoding, so even an hour of gameplay converts quickly and loses nothing. Other picture codecs are re-encoded to H.264, and sound becomes AAC when it isn't already.

features.title: Private
features.text: Your recordings and downloads are converted by your browser; nothing is sent to a server.

features.title: Fast remux
features.text: H.264 picture is copied, not re-encoded, so a long OBS recording becomes an MP4 in a fraction of its length.

features.title: Ready for editors
features.text: The MP4 opens in Premiere, DaVinci Resolve, iMovie and on phones and TVs.

stepsTitle: How to convert MKV to MP4

steps.title: Choose the MKV file
steps.text: Choose or drop a .mkv file from OBS or a download.

steps.title: Check the plan
steps.text: The line above the button says whether the picture is copied, as for most OBS recordings, or re-encoded. Subtitles are left out.

steps.title: Convert and download
steps.text: Click Convert to MP4, play the result, then download it.

handles: MKV from OBS Studio, capture cards and downloads.
H.264 picture: copied into the MP4 untouched.
H.265, VP9 and AV1 picture: re-encoded to H.264 when your browser can play them.
Sound: AAC is kept; other sound your browser can play, such as Opus or MP3, becomes AAC.
limits: Subtitles and chapters are not carried over to the MP4.
H.265, VP9 and AV1 picture has to be re-encoded, which takes much longer than a copy.

faq.question: Is my video uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Your MKV is read and converted by your own browser, on your device, and is never sent anywhere. Large recordings stay on your disk the whole time.

faq.question: Why does OBS record to MKV?
faq.answer: If OBS or the computer crashes, an MKV recorded so far still plays, while an unfinished MP4 is unreadable. OBS can remux to MP4 itself; this page does the same from any device, without OBS.

faq.question: Is MKV to MP4 lossless?
faq.answer: When the picture is H.264, as in most OBS recordings, yes: it is copied untouched. The line above the button tells you before you start.

faq.question: What happens to subtitles?
faq.answer: They are left out: the MP4 has the picture and the sound. If you need the subtitles, keep the .srt file next to the MP4 or burn them in with an editor.

faq.question: How long does a big recording take?
faq.answer: A copied H.264 recording takes about as long as reading the file. A re-encoded one depends on its length and your device, and the progress bar shows where it is.
